content:
# Destination URL handling

## What happens when a link is created

When a destination passes the existing URL validation and self-host checks, the link creation service normalizes it immediately before saving the new link:

- The HTTP(S) scheme and host are lowercased. User information, path, retained query text, and fragment are not lowercased.
- The default port is removed: port `80` for HTTP and port `443` for HTTPS. Non-default ports are retained.
- Query parameters whose raw name begins with `utm_` are removed, with case-insensitive matching. Parameters are separated on `&`; the name is the text before the first `=`. Retained parameters keep their original encoded text, order, values, and duplicates. If all parameters are removed, the query string is omitted.

The normalized destination is stored in the new link and appears in its creation response and link details. Redirects use that stored destination. Existing links are not rewritten.

## API usage

Create a link with `POST /api/v1/links`:

```http
POST /api/v1/links HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "longUrl": "HTTPS://Example.COM:443/docs?utm_source=mail&ref=home#intro"
}
```

A successful request returns `201 Created`. For example, the response includes the normalized destination; generated values will vary:

```json
{
  "code": "abc1234",
  "shortUrl": "http://localhost/abc1234",
  "longUrl": "https://example.com/docs?ref=home#intro",
  "createdAt": "2026-10-20T12:00:00Z",
  "expiresAt": null
}
```

The request and response contract is unchanged. Link creation still uses the existing validation and self-host checks.

## Configuration

There is no URL-normalization setting. Normalization is applied automatically when a new link is created; no separate configuration or database migration is required.

## Limitations

- Normalization applies to newly created links only. Existing stored destinations are not updated.
- The idempotency request hash is based on the original request. Reusing a key with a different original request is still a conflict, even if both destinations would normalize to the same URL. An existing idempotent replay returns its previously stored link.
- UTM matching uses the raw parameter name and does not decode it. For example, an encoded name is not treated as a `utm_` name unless its raw text starts with `utm_`.
- The implementation removes parameters split by `&`; it does not otherwise parse or re-encode retained query text. A query with no matching UTM parameter is left unchanged.
- URL validation and self-host checks occur before normalization. Normalization does not make an otherwise invalid or disallowed destination acceptable.
